description: A head of liquidity risk must decide whether to approve a collateral substitution for the bank's central-bank liquidity facility and finalize the collateral amount, release, custody, and settlement controls, with input from collateral risk, legal, treasury operations, and relationship coverage.

shared_context.S1: The bank has $6,000,000 outstanding under a central-bank liquidity facility.
shared_context.S2: The facility currently has $10,000,000 of government bonds pledged as collateral.
shared_context.S3: The bank wants to replace part of the government-bond collateral with investment-grade corporate bonds so that some government bonds can support an upcoming client settlement.
shared_context.S4: The facility requires collateral with a value of at least 1.25 times the outstanding borrowing.
shared_context.S5: Mara makes the binding decision on the substitution.
shared_context.S6: As part of the normal pre-settlement control meeting, Mara asks collateral risk, legal, treasury operations, and relationship coverage to report any relevant requirements before she signs off.
shared_context.S7: This control meeting is a decision gate: after each area gives its report, Mara records the stated requirements and makes the decision; no additional work-product confirmation is required during the meeting unless an area reports a directly unresolved blocker.

PF1.text: Elias identified a qualifying corporate-bond basket this morning with a market value of exactly $9,400,000 and a required 20% collateral haircut; the basket analysis is complete but has not yet been uploaded to the facility file.

PF2.text: Nadia found in the facility agreement this week that substituted corporate bonds must be limited to a maximum 30% exposure to any one issuer and require a signed collateral-amendment acknowledgment before settlement; she has not yet circulated the clause to the treasury team.

PF3.text: Victor confirmed with the custodian this morning that this substitution can settle only through a segregated custody account and must complete within 2 business days; the custodian confirmation is still in his working email.

PF4.text: Leila's client settlement instructions, received yesterday, require exactly $9,000,000 of government bonds to be released on 2026-08-19; she recorded the instruction in her coverage notes but has not updated the collateral release queue.

acceptance_conditions: The collateral substitution must be approved.
Exactly $9,000,000 of government bonds must be released on 2026-08-19.
Exactly $9,400,000 of corporate bonds must be pledged.
The corporate-bond collateral haircut must be set at exactly 20%.
Single-issuer exposure in the corporate-bond basket must be capped at exactly 30%.
The substitution must use a segregated custody account and settle within 2 business days.
A signed collateral-amendment acknowledgment must be required before settlement.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the decision cannot set the corporate pledge to exactly $9,400,000 or the haircut to exactly 20%, and the facility file offers no verified basis for approving the substitution.
Without PF2, the settlement would not impose the exact 30% single-issuer cap or require the signed collateral-amendment acknowledgment before settlement.
Without PF3, the substitution plan would have no basis for choosing a segregated custody account or setting the settlement window to no more than 2 business days.
Without PF4, the release plan would not specify exactly $9,000,000 of government bonds or the required 2026-08-19 release date.
